Document: DOC-PRD-A-01
Status: SUPERSEDED. Version 1.0, last modified 2026-02-02. This version was replaced by DOC-PRD-A-01-v2 and is retained for history only. Do not implement from this document. Author: Senior Product Manager
Product: Meridian (PROD-A) Defines how a new employee becomes payroll-ready, including the progressive collection of tax and banking details. Reduce the number of steps a new employee must complete before they can reach a working product, while keeping every mandatory compliance step enforced. This document does not cover manager approval workflows or payroll export formatting. Those are specified separately. Tax documentation must be collected after the employee's first successful login, not as part of initial account registration. This requirement is normative for Meridian. Where another document disagrees, this statement takes precedence. An employee must not be granted payment privileges until identity verification has succeeded. This requirement is normative for Meridian. Where another document disagrees, this statement takes precedence. Measured as: completion rate of the compliance steps, time to first productive action, and support contact volume in the first week. How many days should elapse before the tax step is requested? The current answer of three days is provisional.
heading_path: Meridian employee onboarding and payroll readiness
REQ-A-01: Tax details are collected progressively
REQ-A-02: Identity is verified before payment privileges

Document: DOC-PRD-A-02
Status: current. Version 1.0. Last modified 2026-04-10. Author: Product Manager
Product: Meridian (PROD-A) Covers bulk timesheet approval and recurring payroll file export to external payroll providers. Reduce the number of steps a new employee must complete before they can reach a working product, while keeping every mandatory compliance step enforced. This document does not cover manager approval workflows or payroll export formatting. Those are specified separately. A manager must be able to approve multiple timesheets in one action where all selected timesheets are complete. This requirement is normative for Meridian. Where another document disagrees, this statement takes precedence. Payroll exports must run on a fixed, pre-configured schedule and must not be triggered ad hoc by end users. This requirement is normative for Meridian. Where another document disagrees, this statement takes precedence. Measured as: completion rate of the compliance steps, time to first productive action, and support contact volume in the first week. How many days should elapse before the tax step is requested? The current answer of three days is provisional.
heading_path: Meridian manager approval and payroll export
REQ-A-03: Managers approve timesheets in bulk
REQ-A-04: Payroll exports follow a fixed schedule

Decided: 2026-07-16
Decided by: Senior Product Manager Move tax collection to day three of the onboarding ramp rather than requiring it during sign-up. Early testing showed the long sign-up form caused abandonment in the first session. Asking later, once the user has seen value, raised completion of the tax step from 54% to 88%. FEAT-A-01 (Progressive Profiling).

Document: DOC-RBK-A-01
Component: COMP-06 (TaxBand Rate Service)
Owner: external vendor
Last reviewed: 2026-08-05 1. A 429 from the rate service means the 20 calls/minute budget is exhausted. 2. Back off for 30 seconds, then retry the single call. Do not retry the batch. 3. If three consecutive batches fail, raise an operations alert; the tax step cannot complete without resolved rates. Resolves tax bands for a given jurisdiction. Rate-limited, 20 calls/min.
heading_path: Runbook: TaxBand rate service: handling rate-limit responses
